newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Blue chips drive Moroccan bourse higher.
newsitem.headline: Blue chips drive Moroccan bourse higher.

text.p: The Casablanca stock market closed higher on Wednesday driven by heavy trading of the market blue ships, stockbrokers said.
The all-share index closed at 425.05 points, up 1.06 percent.
The banking index closed at 500.55 points, up 1.83 percent on Tuesday. The largest increase was recorded by blue chip Wafabank, which gained 18 dirhams to close at 484 dirhams.

"The bank still trades at 12 times expected 1996 earnings which is at discount to the banking's average. To be noted, the sector stands at 16.5 times," said Anas Alami, head of research at the Casablanca-based Upline Securities.

ONA Group, Morocco's largest private conglomerate, continued its upward trend to close at 440 dirhams, up 13 dirhams on the previous session. Upline Securities forecasts that ONA's 1996 net income will reach 750 million dirhams, or 42 dirhams a share, compared with 35 dirhams a share in 1995, Alami said.
On the other side, bourse trading was marked by low liquidity against strong domestic demand fuelled by an expected positive gross domestic product growth this year, Alami added.
With a record cereal output of 9.75 million tonnes this year, Morocco's economy is expected to grow by more than 11 percent at end 1996, officials said.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, one of the largest market capitalisation companies, rose five dirhams to close at 580 dirhams.
Banque Commerciale du Maroc, one of the most demanded stocks, pursued its rise to close at 740 dirhams, up 14 dirhams on the previous session.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, one the liquid stocks, gained nine dirhams to close at 416 dirhams.
Morocco has eight banks listed on the Casablanca stock market, including a Spanish-Moroccan Uniban.
The bourse total volume rose to 56.3 million dirhams from 23.9 million dirhams on Tuesday due mainly to over the counter trading, stockbrokers said.
